g.text: Packets are getting lost on the way to or from 203.0.113.10.
We found 1 problem affecting your network, and no sign of an attack. This looks like an ordinary fault
Packets are getting lost on the way to or from 203.0.113.10
5.0% of TCP data packets (56 of 1,122) had to be sent again, mostly on both sides of this capture point.
When a packet is lost, TCP notices that the other side never confirmed it and sends it
again (a retransmission). Each resend costs time, and TCP also slows down on purpose because it assumes
the network is overloaded, so pages load slowly and downloads crawl. Losses are spread over both sides of
the capture point (53.6% near the local devices, 46.4% towards 203.0.113.10), which points to general
congestion rather than one bad link.
Like a phone call where every so often a word drops out and you have to say the sentence again, and you
start talking slower to be understood.
Congestion or a faulty link somewhere on the path; the evidence does not pin it to one side.
1. On the affected device, check the link first: for Wi-Fi move closer to the access point or try a
cable; for Ethernet swap the cable and switch port.
rising CRC/FCS errors or drops confirm a bad link, and a duplex mismatch shows up as late collisions
3. Measure the path loss beyond the capture point:
(Windows); loss that starts at one hop and continues to the end shows where it begins.
4. Check whether the Internet uplink is saturated (router traffic graphs); if it is, enable QoS/SQM on
the router or reduce the load.
5. Check the router/switch logs for interface errors or flapping links during the capture window.
Why we think it's a fault
5.0% of data segments were retransmitted across 2 connections
Normal TCP recovery behaviour (14 fast and 42 timeout retransmissions): endpoints are reacting to
637 duplicate ACKs: receivers report missing data
